name: Builder Operations Stage Analysis Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for a Threat Model Spec Analysis Report produced at the Builder Operations PDLC stage.

categories.name: Detection Coverage
categories.description: Whether detection capability is assessed against the actual techniques relevant to this product, not a generic checklist.

options.label: Pass
criteria: Detection coverage assessed for the specific techniques a Builder Definition threat model identified as relevant

options.label: Partial
criteria: Generic detection coverage stated without connecting to this product's actual threats

categories.evaluationPrompt: Is detection coverage assessed against the techniques this specific product's threat model identifies, not a generic industry checklist?

categories.name: Incident Evidence Grounding
categories.description: Whether findings that reference an incident actually cite it as evidence.

options.label: Pass
criteria: Every incident-related Finding cites the incident Artifact as Evidence

options.label: Partial
criteria: Incident referenced narratively without a formal Evidence citation

options.label: Fail
criteria: Incident findings with no supporting evidence at all

categories.evaluationPrompt: When the report discusses an incident, does the relevant Finding cite the incident artifact as Evidence?

categories.name: Dynamic Testing Disclosure
categories.description: Whether the report explicitly states if dynamic testing (DAST/pen test/red team) was in scope, so its absence is never silently read as a clean result.

options.label: Pass
criteria: Report explicitly states whether dynamic testing was performed and, if not, that it was out of scope for this run

options.label: Partial
criteria: Dynamic testing status implied but not stated explicitly

options.label: Fail
criteria: No mention of dynamic testing scope at all — absence could be misread as 'nothing found'

categories.evaluationPrompt: Does the report explicitly state whether dynamic testing was in scope for this analysis run, so a reader can't mistake silence for a clean bill of health?

categories.name: Control Effectiveness
categories.description: Whether findings assess whether existing controls actually work, not just whether they exist.

options.label: Pass
criteria: Findings assess whether controls detect/prevent in practice, with supporting evidence

options.label: Partial
criteria: Controls listed as present but effectiveness not assessed

categories.evaluationPrompt: Do findings assess whether operational controls actually detect or prevent the threats they're meant to address, not just that they exist on paper?
